result.document_summary: Boston.gov page describing the Housing Stability Notification Act, which requires landlords ending a tenancy to give tenants a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources and to notify the City.
result.notes: The Act is a notice-and-reporting requirement for tenancy terminations; it does not restrict eviction causes or halt eviction. It is nonetheless the closest in-scope item (just_cause_eviction: notice requirements for ending a tenancy), so one record is output with moderate confidence. The page gives no effective date and no coverage exemptions. Rent increase, deposit, fee, screening and algorithm rules are not present.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act - notice of tenants' rights and City reporting on tenancy termination
rules.requirement: A landlord planning to end a tenancy must deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice, and must submit the notice and tenant contact information to the City through its online portal. A violation does not halt the eviction process.
rules.key_value: Warning for 1st offense; $300 per day for 2nd and subsequent offenses
rules.citation: City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act requires
ALL LANDLORDS
planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords in Boston who plan to end a tenancy agreement.
